b.d: American Gemological Laboratories, New York; coloured-stone reports.
American Gem Society trade body with its own grading laboratory, AGS Laboratories, founded 1996.
Chatsworth, California maker of polyurethane casts of skulls and skeletons, including hominid fossils.
Company that produced and sold the first synthetic moissanite gems, introduced to jewellery in 1998.
Company founded by Carroll Chatham; first marketable synthetic emerald, also synthetic ruby and sapphire.
Camden taxidermy firm that supplied museums; closed 1965 or 1967.
Non-profit gemological institute and grading laboratory; set the D–Z colour scale used worldwide.
Gemresearch Swisslab; coloured-stone and origin reports.
Swiss laboratory known for coloured-stone origin reports.
Diamond laboratory in Antwerp, certifying diamonds.
International Gemological Institute; certifies diamonds, coloured stones and jewellery, widely used for lab-grown diamonds.
Association of meteorite collectors and dealers with a code of ethics and a dealer-verification scheme.
Calgary-based miner and the largest commercial producer of gem ammolite, supplying over 90% of it.
Seattle seller of element density cubes, ampules, Lucite cubes and display cases for collectors.
Learned society whose Nomenclature Committee approves meteorite names and classifications in the Meteoritical Bulletin Database.
Tokyo pearl jeweller founded by Kōkichi Mikimoto, pioneer of cultured Akoya pearls.
Major producer of South Sea pearls off north-western Australia.
London taxidermy firm of Piccadilly, known for game mounts and Records of Big Game.
Oklahoma City supplier of real and replica skulls and skeletons, with beetle cleaning services.
Swiss Gemmological Institute in Basel, part of the Swiss Foundation for Gemstone Research; origin reports for coloured stones and pearls.
Crystal maker in Wattens, Tyrol, founded in 1895 by Daniel Swarovski; its first figurine was a stylised mouse.
Bangalore taxidermy firm founded by William Tocher, closed in the 1960s.
Mysore taxidermy firm that mounted tens of thousands of tiger and leopard trophies.
Sussex taxidermist (1835–1918) whose dressed-animal dioramas were sold at Bonhams in 2003.
